test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 2 Feb 2021 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is correct about International Space Station (ISS)?

options.text: It is expected to operate until 2050.
It has been assembled mainly by USA and China
Only astronauts from USA and China are allowed to visit ISS.
It is located in low earth orbit.

solution:
The correct answer is __**It is located in low earth orbit**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The International Space Station **is the **largest modular space station **currently in **low Earth orbit**.
 
• It is **a multinational collaborative project **involving **five participating space agencies**: NASA, Roscosmos, JAXA, ESA, and CSA.
 
• The **space station **is jointly **run by **the space agencies of **Russia, the U.S., Europe, Japan and Canada**.
 
• The **first piece **was put in **orbit in 1998**, and the **outpost has been continuously inhabited for nearly 22 years**.
 
• It is **used to conduct scientific research **in **zero gravity **and **test out equipment **for **future space journeys**.
 
• The **mission **of the **International Space Station **is to enable **long-term exploration **of **space **and **provide benefits to people on Earth**.
 
• With **six state-of-the-art laboratories**, the Space Station will be **the premiere research facility **in space, **four times larger **and more **capable **than any **previous space station**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The International Space Station **was taken into **space piece-by-piece **and **gradually built **in orbit using **spacewalking astronauts **and **robotics**.
 
• **Most missions **used **NASA's space shuttle **to carry up the **heavier pieces**, although some individual modules were launched on single-use rockets.
 
• **Several systems **are currently used on **board the ISS to maintain the spacecraft's atmosphere**, which is **similar to the Earth's.**
